title: The Bell
subtitle: Days 13–16: a fallen church camp, a Friday market, and the siren that walks the dead

setting.name: The West County and Harmon Siding, Days 13–16
setting.description: By the second week the county has sorted itself out. The power is gone and the national radio went silent on Day 9. Kettering's on Front Street holds the party, Dr. Brooks's clinic and whoever they have taken in. The Co-op at Harmon Siding holds the bridge, the fuel, the grain and about eleven hundred people, and runs a barter market every Friday. Out west, the Mennonite farms on Prairie Hill hold thirty families who have wells, horses, root cellars and a deep reluctance to shoot anyone; the Lutheran church camp at Dutch Hollow held sixty more, until the night of Day 12. The Co-op has issued every holdout in the county a typed 'Notice of Assessment': one-fifth of all food, fuel, medicine and ammunition each week, plus labour, in exchange for 'protection'. Dutch Hollow refused on Day 9. This scenario is the party finding out what protection means.
setting.atmosphere: Autumn turning: soybeans gone gold and unharvested, the first cold nights, woodsmoke, geese going over. The dead are fewer in the countryside and more frightening for it — you see one at a time, a long way off across a field, walking. The Co-op Market is the most cheerful place the players have been since Ferry Days: music from a battery radio, kids, trade, coffee for the first time in a week, and Colleen Marsh walking among her people shaking hands. The horror of this scenario is not the dead. It is a typed ledger, a tornado siren bolted to a grain truck, and a reasonable woman explaining her arithmetic.

keyLocations.name: Dutch Hollow Church Camp
keyLocations.description: A Lutheran summer camp in a wooded hollow off County Road K: a timber chapel with a small bell tower, a dining hall, eight cabins, a caretaker's house, a swimming pond and one gravel road in. Sixty people from Corbin's Ferry and Haskett sheltered here from Day 3. On the night of Day 12 a Horde came down the road out of nowhere and through the gate.
features: The camp gate is chained and padlocked from the inside — and the chain has been cut from the outside with bolt cutters, cleanly (Investigation DC 12)
Tyre tracks in the mud of the camp road: dual rear wheels, a heavy truck, which came as far as the gate, turned in the clearing, and went back the way it came (Survival DC 13)
On the dining hall noticeboard, under the camp rota: a typed Co-op NOTICE OF ASSESSMENT dated Day 9, and under it, in marker, the camp director's reply: 'No thank you. We are doing fine. God bless.'
encounters: A Horde still in the camp — the sixty, and what came for them
Caleb Voss, 14, alive in the chapel bell tower since the night before last, with the ladder pulled up
secrets: Caleb heard it: at about 2 a.m. a siren — 'like the tornado siren at school' — getting louder along County Road K, stopping at the gate, then going away again. Then the dead came, hundreds of them, following the sound down the road. He saw headlights. He saw a grain truck with something big and grey bolted on the back

The caretaker's house has what the safehouse has needed since Day 1: a deer-season reloading setup with smokeless powder, 400 primers and boxes of sorted brass — enough to reload 300 rounds of 9mm, .38 or 5.56mm at the Kettering bench (see Ammunition Is What You Have)

keyLocations.name: Prairie Hill
keyLocations.description: Thirty Mennonite farm families on a long rise west of the river: white farmhouses, bank barns, windmills and wells, a meetinghouse, a one-room school, and fields worked with draft horses. They had no electricity to lose. They have food, water, livestock, and no guns except a few deer rifles nobody likes to bring out.
features: Wells and hand pumps, root cellars full for winter, a smokehouse, a forge — the most self-sufficient place in the county
Bishop Amos Weaver's farm at the crest, with a view down County Road K for two miles in each direction
The community will trade food for feed bags, salt, medicine and labour — and they need the feed from Kettering's badly
encounters: Bishop Amos Weaver and the brethren: social, and a hard ask
A Zombie Shambler or two wandering the field edges, put down quietly with a hay fork by a farmer who will not discuss it
secrets: Prairie Hill received its own Notice of Assessment on Day 11 with a deadline of Day 15. Nadine Coyle, the community's midwife, privately asked the Co-op for protection on Day 4, when a Horde passed close, and the Co-op has a copy of her signed request. It reads as consent
The bishop will not fight. He will not pay the tithe either: one-fifth of everything is how families starve by February. He intends to refuse, and to pray

keyLocations.name: The Co-op Market at Harmon Siding
keyLocations.description: Every Friday the Co-op opens the gravel lot between the scale house and the elevator to anyone who has registered: folding tables, pickup tailgates, a chalkboard of barter rates, a coffee urn, a man with a fiddle. Inside the perimeter fence: the elevator and its bins, the fuel depot, the rail spur with forty stranded grain hoppers, the Co-op office, a motor pool in the old equipment shed, and family housing in the hoppers and the machine shop.
features: The chalkboard of barter rates (use the Scarcity and Barter rule exactly: the Co-op wrote it)
The motor pool: grain trucks, pickups, a fuel tanker and, under a tarp at the back of the equipment shed, one truck nobody is allowed near
The Co-op office in the scale house: Colleen Marsh's desk, a county map with coloured pins, and a green ledger
encounters: Colleen Marsh, in person, gracious and very interested in the party
Co-op guards everywhere (Gang Enforcer) and a Sniper on the elevator head house; this is not a place to start a fight
secrets: The truck under the tarp is THE BELL: a Co-op grain truck with a Federal Signal 2001 tornado siren (salvaged from the Haskett fire station) bolted to a steel frame on the bed, a 7,000-watt generator, and the cab windows plated with steel. Wade Pruitt runs it

The green ledger lists every holdout in the county, its headcount, its assessment, and its status. Dutch Hollow's line reads: 'Refused 9/27. Rung 9/30.' Prairie Hill's reads: 'Notice 9/29. Deadline 10/3.' (Day 1 was Saturday September 19.)
The map's black pins are 'collection sites' — and one of them is Sullivan Ridge Quarry

keyLocations.name: Sullivan Ridge Quarry
keyLocations.description: A flooded limestone quarry in the timber south-west of Prairie Hill: sheer 60-foot walls, a gravel haul road down to a wide floor at the shallow end, a chain-link gate and a scale shack at the top.
features: The quarry floor is a pen. The Co-op's 'wranglers' have been driving the dead into it for a week with a speaker truck, and closing the haul road behind them with a steel gate and two shipping containers
About three hundred dead in the pit — six Hordes' worth — milling at the bottom, quiet unless something makes a noise above
A loudspeaker on a pole at the top of the haul road, wired to a car battery in the scale shack
encounters: Two Co-op wranglers in the scale shack (Gang Enforcer), bored and armed
The pen itself, if anybody is foolish enough to open the gate or go down
secrets: The quarry pen is the Co-op's reserve. Wade opens the gate, the Bell plays, and three hundred dead follow it wherever it goes. This is what will be pointed at Prairie Hill on the night of Day 15

A party that blocks the haul road (the shipping containers can be shoved with a truck, Piloting DC 14; or the road can be dropped with a charge, if anyone has one) makes the pen useless to the Co-op for the rest of the campaign

keyLocations.name: County Road K
keyLocations.description: Eleven miles of gravel from Harmon Siding west past Sullivan Ridge, Dutch Hollow and Prairie Hill: fence lines, ditches, a single-lane bridge over Cutter Creek, and two farmsteads abandoned since Day 2.
features: The Cutter Creek bridge: a one-lane steel bridge 30 feet over a dry creek bed; the only way a heavy truck can get from the quarry to Prairie Hill
The abandoned Lindell farm: a house, a machine shed, a grain bin, and a hay loft with a clear line of fire down 500 yards of road
Gravel carries sound. On a still night you can hear an engine two miles off
encounters: The night of Day 15: the Bell, its two escort pickups, and three hundred dead walking behind it
secrets: The Bell has to cross the Cutter Creek bridge. A truck stopped on it blocks it; a bridge with its deck planks pulled cannot take a grain truck at all (an hour's work with crowbars and three people)
If the Bell is stopped and silenced on County Road K, the dead behind it lose the sound and drift — toward whatever else is loud

synopsis: Day 13. The safehouse is down to six days of Supplies after taking in Dr. Brooks's people, and the Mennonite community on Prairie Hill has food and needs the feed in Kettering's back room. While the party is trading there, word comes that the Dutch Hollow church camp — sixty people — was overrun the night before last. The party goes to look and finds a cut gate chain, heavy truck tracks, a Co-op Notice of Assessment the camp refused, and a fourteen-year-old boy in the bell tower who heard a tornado siren come down the road in the middle of the night, and the dead come after it. On Friday, Day 14, the party goes to the Co-op Market at Harmon Siding to trade, to listen and to look. Colleen Marsh meets them in person, offers them membership — she wants the medic and the tech, and says so — and tells them, without any embarrassment at all, that Prairie Hill's deadline is tomorrow. In the motor pool is a grain truck with a siren bolted on its bed; in her office is a green ledger with Dutch Hollow's line marked 'Rung'; on her map is a black pin at Sullivan Ridge Quarry, where three hundred dead are penned. Prairie Hill will not pay and will not fight. On the night of Day 15, the Bell comes down County Road K with three hundred dead walking behind it, and the party is all that stands between it and thirty farm families.
hook: Day 13, mid-morning, a wagon at the back of Kettering's: a woman in a dark dress and a black head-covering, driving two Belgian draft horses, with a shotgun across her knees that she clearly regards as a tool for snakes. 'I'm Nadine Coyle,' she says. 'I deliver babies on Prairie Hill. We hear you have feed and a doctor. We have food.' It is a good trade and everyone knows it. She stays for coffee — the safehouse has none, so she has brought some — and, at the end, almost as an afterthought, she says: 'Dutch Hollow's gone. The camp. Night before last. My cousin's boy was there.' She looks into her cup. 'We heard a siren. Out on the K road, in the middle of the night. Nobody has a siren any more. Do they?'

acts.title: Act 1: Dutch Hollow
acts.description: Trade at Prairie Hill, then investigate the fallen camp. Clear it, find the evidence, find Caleb, and take the reloading supplies. Ends with the party knowing the Horde was brought.
objectives: Make the feed-for-food trade with Prairie Hill (Supplies +30 person-days)
Reach Dutch Hollow and clear enough of it to search
Find the evidence: cut chain, truck tracks, the Notice of Assessment
Find Caleb Voss and hear what he heard
Recover the reloading supplies from the caretaker's house
encounters: A Horde in the camp grounds; 1d4 Zombie Shamblers in the dining hall; a Zombie Brute (the camp director's son, a college wrestler) in the chapel
An Infected Animal: the camp's farm dog, turned, in the cabins

scenes.name: Prairie Hill
scenes.description: A barter scene with people who have never used money much and do not intend to start. Establish Bishop Weaver, the community, and the Notice of Assessment they have also received.
scenes.readAloud: "Prairie Hill looks like nothing has happened. That is the first thing and it is almost unbearable. White farmhouses, red bank barns, laundry on the line, a windmill turning, a boy driving four horses and a harrow across a field in a perfectly straight line. Then you see the fence at the edge of the field has been doubled with hog panel, and there is a man on the barn roof with binoculars, and on the meetinghouse door, fixed with a tack, is a typed sheet of paper with the Co-op's letterhead. Bishop Amos Weaver, a small white-bearded man in braces and a straw hat, meets you at the gate and shakes each of your hands. 'You are welcome,' he says. 'We have read the paper on the door. We would like to know what you think it means.'"

skillChecks.success: Forty bags of feed and a box of antibiotics buy 30 person-days of Supplies, two laying hens, and the community's goodwill. Prairie Hill will shelter the party if it ever has to.
skillChecks.failure: The trade still happens, but at 20 person-days; the brethren are polite and careful.

skillChecks.success: The bishop has decided to refuse the assessment and is frightened of what that means. Nadine Coyle, standing behind him, is more frightened still, and is not looking at him.

scenes.roleplayNotes: Prairie Hill is what the party is fighting for in Act 3. Make it real: a name, a face, a child, a meal. The bishop's position is principled and not stupid: one-fifth of everything every week starves a community by February. He will not fight. He will accept help.

scenes.name: The Camp
scenes.description: Dutch Hollow on the afternoon of Day 13. A dead place in a pretty hollow.
scenes.readAloud: "Dutch Hollow is a camp you can imagine full of children: a hand-painted sign, WELCOME HOME, over the gate, cabins named after apostles, a canoe rack by the pond, a chapel with a white bell tower. The gate is standing open. The chain is lying in the gravel. There is a hymnal on the road, and a single shoe, and further in, in the field by the dining hall, perhaps forty figures standing quite still in the morning sun, all facing the same direction — back up the road, toward the way they came, as if they are still waiting for something to call them."

skillChecks.success: The chain was cut from the outside with bolt cutters, cleanly. Nobody inside opened this gate.
skillChecks.failure: The gate is open. Someone opened it. You do not see which side.

skillChecks.success: Dual rear wheels, a heavy truck, the night before last: it came to the gate, turned in the clearing, and left. Hundreds of footprints come down the road behind it and do not go back.
skillChecks.failure: A mess of tracks; a lot of feet.

skillChecks.success: Up in the bell tower, a shutter moves, and then a very small amount of a pale face.
skillChecks.failure: The bell tower is quiet. (Caleb sees you; he will ring the bell once, softly, when you are close — +1 Attention.)

enemies: A Horde in the field by the dining hall
1d4 Zombie Shamblers in the dining hall
Infected Animal (the camp dog) in the cabins
combatEncounters.tactics: The camp can be taken a piece at a time, quietly, from the woods, or loudly and all at once. The Horde in the field responds to anything at Attention 3 or higher. The Brute is in the chapel at the foot of the bell-tower ladder, beating on the wall; it has been doing it for two days. The dog comes fast and alone.
combatEncounters.terrain: Timber cabins (wood: half cover vs. pistols, none vs. rifles), the stone chimney of the dining hall (full cover), the pond (the dead wade in and do not come out quickly), the tree line (heavily obscured beyond 30 feet).

scenes.roleplayNotes: This is the scenario's grief scene. The sixty were townspeople the players might know: a teacher, a family from the festival, the Lions Club man. Every one of them is standing in that field. If the players knew Rosa Jimenez's son was here (ob-scenario-002), he was. Caleb Voss, when they get him down, is dehydrated and very calm in the way of a boy in shock. He tells them about the siren and the truck in a flat voice and then falls asleep in the middle of a sentence.
loot: Caretaker's house: smokeless powder and primers (400), sorted brass — enough to reload 300 rounds at the Kettering bench
Dining hall pantry: canned goods (25 person-days)
Camp office: the Notice of Assessment and the director's reply

acts.title: Act 2: Market Day
acts.description: Friday, Day 14, at the Co-op Market at Harmon Siding. Trade, meet Colleen Marsh, find the Bell and the ledger, and — if they want proof — scout Sullivan Ridge Quarry.
objectives: Meet Colleen Marsh and hear her offer
Find the truck under the tarp
See the green ledger and the map
encounters: Colleen Marsh: social; she is the most dangerous person in the county and she is not hiding it
Infiltrating the motor pool and the office: Stealth, Sleight of Hand, Deception and Computers
Sullivan Ridge Quarry: two wranglers (Gang Enforcer) and three hundred dead in a pit

scenes.name: The Market
scenes.description: Barter, coffee, children, music. The Co-op at its best.
scenes.readAloud: "The gravel lot under the elevator is full of people for the first time since Ferry Days. Pickup tailgates down. Folding tables of canned goods, batteries, seed corn, chickens in crates, a woman selling haircuts for two rounds of .22. Somebody is playing a fiddle by the scale house and a dozen kids are chasing each other round the fuel tanks while a man in a hi-vis vest pretends not to see. A chalkboard on an easel reads TODAY'S RATES, and under it, neatly: 1 RD PISTOL = 1 DAY FOOD. 1 GAL FUEL = 5 RDS. ANTIBIOTICS 10-DAY = 50 RDS. CASH NOT ACCEPTED. There is coffee. It is real. A tall woman in a canvas barn coat and reading glasses is walking slowly through the crowd, shaking hands, asking after people's children by name."

skillChecks.success: Good trades: the GM improves one barter rate in the party's favour by a fifth for the day.
skillChecks.failure: Market rates, and the Co-op's trader takes his time.

skillChecks.success: The market talks: the Co-op 'took care of' a gang that tried to rob the fuel depot on Day 6; holdouts that pay are doing fine; nobody here says the words Dutch Hollow, and when you do, the conversation ends.
skillChecks.failure: Pleasant small talk. People are happy here.

scenes.roleplayNotes: Let the players enjoy this. It is the Co-op's argument made in coffee and children: this works. Travis Kemper is here if he survived ob-scenario-002; if they made a deal with him, he is grateful and nervous and will not meet their eyes when they ask about Dutch Hollow. Wade Pruitt is not here — he 'works nights'.

scenes.name: Colleen
scenes.description: Colleen Marsh invites the party into the scale-house office for coffee. She makes an offer and explains her arithmetic. She does not mention the Bell, and she does not deny it if asked directly.
scenes.readAloud: "The Co-op office is a scale house with a window onto the truck scale and a county map on the wall stuck with coloured pins. Colleen Marsh pours coffee from a thermos into mugs that say HASKETT FARMERS CO-OP — 75 YEARS. She is in her fifties, with grey hair in a practical braid and a quartermaster's way of counting things with her eyes while she talks. 'This county had twenty-six thousand people three weeks ago,' she says. 'I think it has about two thousand now. I have one point eight million bushels of corn and beans, forty thousand gallons of fuel, and a water plant. That feeds twelve hundred people through to next harvest if nobody wastes anything and nobody gets greedy. Not two thousand. Twelve hundred.' She sets down the thermos. 'I'd like your medic and your mechanic. I'd like all of you, frankly. I'm told you're good.'"

skillChecks.success: Every word is true, and she believes all of it. She has already decided who the twelve hundred are, and she sleeps fine.
skillChecks.failure: She is the most competent person you have met since Day 1, and she is offering you a place.

skillChecks.success: She agrees to extend Prairie Hill's deadline by a week 'as a courtesy to you', which buys time but does not change her mind. (A Face can attempt this with Read the Room first: her fear is February, and her lie is that she has a choice.)
skillChecks.failure: 'Tomorrow,' she says, kindly. 'I hope they'll see sense. It's a good community. I'd hate to lose it.'

skillChecks.success: While she pours, you read the ledger open on her desk: Dutch Hollow — 'Refused 9/27. Rung 9/30.' Prairie Hill — 'Notice 9/29. Deadline 10/3.' Kettering's (Front St.) — 'A-list: 2. Monitor.'
skillChecks.failure: She closes the ledger, without hurry, as she sits down.

scenes.roleplayNotes: Colleen Marsh is not a cackling villain and must not be played as one. She is a retired Army logistics officer who did two tours moving fuel and food through places that were trying to kill her, and she has taken the county's survival as a logistics problem with one acceptable answer. She does not enjoy what the Bell does. She regards it as cheaper than bullets and kinder than starving. If the party asks her directly about Dutch Hollow, she says: 'They were offered the same terms as everyone. I don't run a charity, and I can't feed people who won't help.' She will not admit to the Bell in words. She will not threaten the party in her own office; she does not need to. If the party argues Prairie Hill's case, she produces, from the ledger, a clipboard sheet signed by Nadine Coyle on Day 4 requesting Co-op protection, and says, mildly, that Prairie Hill asked her first. If Nadine is present, every character makes an Insight DC 10: she is mortified, and it is true.

scenes.name: The Truck Under the Tarp
scenes.description: The motor pool at the back of the equipment shed: the Bell.
scenes.readAloud: "It is a grain truck — a Co-op tandem, white, with the Co-op's wheat-sheaf logo on the door — and the tarp over its bed is hiding something tall. When you lift the corner you see a steel frame welded to the bed, a fat diesel generator, a tangle of heavy cable, and, on top of it all, bolted to a post, the big grey drum of a civil-defence tornado siren with the stencil HASKETT FIRE DEPT. still on its housing. The cab windows have been covered in welded steel plate with slits cut to see through. On the dashboard someone has taped a laminated card in neat capitals: ROUTE K — QUARRY GATE — CUTTER CR. BRIDGE — RUN SLOW — DO NOT STOP IN TIMBER."

skillChecks.success: In and out of the motor pool without a guard looking twice.
skillChecks.failure: A guard sees you near the tarp. Deception DC 14 to explain, or the party is escorted out of the Market — and Colleen knows.

skillChecks.success: You could sabotage it: a cut fuel line in the generator, a loosened bolt on the siren rotor. It will fail 1d4 minutes after it is switched on, wherever it happens to be.
skillChecks.failure: You can see how it works. You cannot get at it quietly.

skillChecks.success: The siren's cable runs to a switch in the cab. Turn the switch off and the siren winds down over a round. That is all it takes to silence the Bell — if you are in the cab.
skillChecks.failure: It is loud. It is a siren. That is what you know.

scenes.roleplayNotes: Do not let this become a firefight inside the Co-op perimeter: thirty guards and a Sniper make that suicide, and the GM should say so plainly. The players should leave knowing exactly what the Bell is, where it goes, and that it goes on Saturday night.

scenes.name: The Pen
scenes.description: Optional. Sullivan Ridge Quarry, scouted from the rim.
scenes.readAloud: "From the timber on the rim of the quarry you look down sixty feet of sheer grey limestone into a pit with green water at one end and a wide gravel floor at the other, and the gravel floor is moving. They are packed in shoulder to shoulder, hundreds of them, farm clothes and church clothes and hi-vis vests and a few in Guard fatigues, and they are quiet, almost peaceful, swaying in the sun. Up the haul road, at the top, two men in Co-op caps are sitting on lawn chairs outside a scale shack, playing cards, next to a loudspeaker on a pole."

skillChecks.success: You get close enough to the shack to take the two wranglers without a shot — or to listen to them talk about Saturday.
skillChecks.failure: They see you. They have a radio, and they use it.

skillChecks.success: With a truck, the two shipping containers at the head of the haul road can be shoved over the edge and into the road cut. The pen is sealed for good. The Bell has nothing to lead on Saturday night except whatever it can collect on the road.
skillChecks.failure: The containers jam halfway; the noise is +3 Attention, and three hundred dead look up.

combatEncounters.tactics: They are bored, half-trained and want to live; they surrender readily. If anyone shoots, remember the pit: Attention rises normally, and at 6 the dead in the pen surge against the gate.
combatEncounters.terrain: The rim (a 60-foot fall: 6d6), the scale shack (wooden), the lawn chairs, the gate.

scenes.roleplayNotes: Sealing the pen is the cleverest single thing the party can do in this scenario. If they do it, Act 3 is a fight with the Bell and its escort and whatever the Bell has collected on the road — one Horde, not six. Reward the thinking, and let Colleen hear about it.
loot: Scale shack: a Co-op handheld radio on the Co-op's channel (the party can now listen in), 12-gauge shells (14), .308 rounds (20)

acts.title: Act 3: The Night of the Bell
acts.description: Saturday, the night of Day 15. Prairie Hill has refused. The Bell comes down County Road K with its escort and the dead walking behind it. Stop it.
objectives: Choose where to stop the Bell: the Cutter Creek bridge, the Lindell farm, or Prairie Hill itself
Silence the Bell before the dead reach Prairie Hill
Deal with Wade Pruitt and the escort
Decide what to do with the Bell, and with Wade
encounters: The Bell (vehicle) and two escort pickups
Wade Pruitt (unique, below) and 6 Co-op escorts (2 Mercenary, 4 Gang Enforcer)
The dead behind the Bell: six Hordes if the pen is open, one Horde if it was sealed, plus Zombie Runners at the front

scenes.name: Saturday Night
scenes.description: The ambush. Run it as a clock: the dead are two minutes behind the Bell, and the Bell moves at 10 miles an hour.
scenes.readAloud: "You hear it before you see it, from three miles away: a long, rising wail across the dark fields, rising and falling, rising and falling, the sound that used to mean get to the basement. Then headlights on the K road, three sets, moving slow. Then — only when the moon comes out from behind a cloud — the road behind the headlights. It is full. Fence line to fence line, as far back as you can see in the moonlight, the road is full of the dead, walking toward the sound, and the sound is walking toward Prairie Hill."

skillChecks.success: The Cutter Creek bridge planks come up in an hour. When the Bell gets there it cannot cross; it stops, and it is a sitting target with three hundred dead coming up behind it.
skillChecks.failure: Half the planks come up. The Bell can cross at a crawl: one round slower, and a DC 13 Piloting check for the driver or it drops a wheel through.

skillChecks.success: You count the escort: Wade in the lead pickup with three men, the Bell, and a second pickup with three more. The Bell's driver is alone.
skillChecks.failure: Headlights and a siren. Some people. Some guns.

enemies: WADE PRUITT (unique, human, Medium): AC 15 (plate carrier); HP 52; speed 30; STR 16 DEX 14 CON 14 INT 11 WIS 13 CHA 14; saves STR +6, CON +5; skills Athletics +6, Intimidation +5, Perception +4; proficiency +3. Former deputy: when Wade takes the Aim bonus action he also grants one ally within 30 ft advantage on their next attack. Brave: advantage on saves against being Suppressed or frightened. Actions — Multiattack: two attacks. AR-15 rifle: +5 to hit, range 120/360, 2d6+2 piercing, magazine 30, 5.56mm rounds (60). Service pistol (Glock 9mm): +5 to hit, range 30/120, 1d8+2 piercing, magazine 15. Rifle butt / fist: +6 to hit, 1d6+3 bludgeoning. Reaction — Cover Me: when an ally within 5 ft is hit, Wade takes the hit instead.

THE BELL (vehicle): AC 12, HP 80, plated cab (the driver has three-quarters cover). The SIREN UNIT on the bed: AC 14, HP 20; a called shot is not needed — it is big — but destroying it with gunfire takes rounds. The CAB SWITCH silences it in one round. The siren is +5 Attention per round within a mile; it is the reason the dead are coming.
The dead: six Hordes (if the pen is open) or one Horde (if the pen was sealed), arriving 2 minutes (20 rounds) after the Bell, led by 1d4+2 Zombie Runners
combatEncounters.difficulty: Deadly if the pen is open and the party stands and fights; Hard otherwise
combatEncounters.tactics: Wade's escort knows the drill: they stay ahead of the dead, they keep the Bell moving, and they will not stop to fight unless forced to. If the Bell is stopped, the escort fights to restart it for 3 rounds, then — as the dead close — tries to get Wade and the driver out in the pickups. Wade will surrender if the Bell is silenced and his people are being shot, and if someone he trusts (Shay, if she is with the party; Travis Kemper, if he is present) asks him to. Once the Bell is silent, the dead lose the sound and drift, and the GM should let them turn toward whatever is now loudest: gunfire, the pickups' engines, or — if anyone has the presence of mind to drive the Bell away and switch it back on somewhere empty — the Bell itself.
combatEncounters.terrain: Gravel road with ditches on both sides (half cover lying in the ditch), barbed-wire fences (difficult terrain; 1d4 slashing to cross quickly), the Cutter Creek bridge (one lane, steel rail: half cover; a 30-foot drop into the dry creek bed), the Lindell farm hay loft (three-quarters cover, a 500-yard line of fire down the road), soybean fields (lightly obscured at night; anything can be in them).

scenes.roleplayNotes: This is the scenario's climax, and the campaign's first open war with the living. The smartest way through it is not a gunfight: it is the cab switch, the bridge planks, the sealed pen, and Wade's surrender. Reward those. If the party captures the Bell, they own the most powerful weapon in the county; let them understand that, and let it frighten them. If Wade dies, he rises in 2d6 minutes. If Shay is there, every character makes the Shaken save.
loot: The Bell itself (the truck, the siren, the generator, Diesel (30 gallons) in its tanks)
Wade Pruitt's AR-15 and 5.56mm rounds (60), Glock 9mm and 9mm rounds (30), plate carrier (tactical vest)
Escort pickups: 2 Ford F-250s with Gasoline (15 gallons) each; 12-gauge shells (18), 9mm rounds (40), .308 rounds (12), a Co-op handheld radio

scenes.name: Morning
scenes.description: Day 16. What the party does with what they have taken.
scenes.readAloud: "At first light the K road is empty except for tyre marks, brass casings in the gravel, and the long trampled swathe where the dead went by. They turned away north, toward the river, following the last loud thing they heard. Prairie Hill is standing. The boy is out with his four horses and the harrow, in the same straight line as before, as if nothing happened, because his father told him the field still needed doing. On the Co-op channel, a calm woman's voice is calling Wade's call-sign, every five minutes, and getting no answer."
scenes.roleplayNotes: End on the radio. Colleen knows. If the party has Wade, they have a prisoner who knows everything about the Co-op — and who is, in his own mind, a decent man who did what he was told. If they have the Bell, they have Colleen's weapon. If they have the green ledger (stolen in Act 2), they have something worse for her: proof. All three matter in ob-scenario-004. Award XP. The party should now be level 5 or close.

npcsInvolved.name: Colleen Marsh, 54
npcsInvolved.role: Co-op general manager / the campaign's antagonist
npcsInvolved.description: Tall, grey braid, reading glasses on a cord, canvas barn coat. Retired Army logistics officer (two tours in Iraq moving fuel), twenty years running the Co-op. Remembers every name. Never raises her voice. Has done the arithmetic and accepted the answer.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Twelve hundred people alive at next harvest. She has decided which twelve hundred, and she will spend anyone else to get there.

npcsInvolved.name: Wade Pruitt, 33
npcsInvolved.role: Co-op checkpoint chief / the Bell's driver
npcsInvolved.description: The friendly face of ob-scenario-002, revealed: he runs the Bell. He believes Dutch Hollow was a tragedy that the camp chose by refusing. He has not slept well since.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Keep his people fed, keep Colleen's trust, find his sister — and never have to look at what comes down the road behind him.

npcsInvolved.name: Bishop Amos Weaver, 70
npcsInvolved.description: Small, white-bearded, braces and straw hat; gentle, immovable, plain-spoken. Will not fight, will not pay, will feed anyone who comes to his door.
npcsInvolved.motivation: That his people live through the winter without becoming something they are not.

npcsInvolved.name: Nadine Coyle, 38
npcsInvolved.description: See her NPC file. Brings the trade and the news of Dutch Hollow. Asked the Co-op for protection on Day 4, which Colleen holds as consent.

npcsInvolved.name: Caleb Voss, 14
npcsInvolved.description: Skinny, freckled, in a youth-group T-shirt, two days in the bell tower with a jug of rainwater. The witness.
npcsInvolved.motivation: His mother was in the camp. He wants someone to tell him it was not his fault for not ringing the bell to warn them; it was not.

npcsInvolved.name: Travis Kemper, 39
npcsInvolved.description: From ob-scenario-002. Knows about Dutch Hollow and has been sick about it since.
npcsInvolved.motivation: If the party made a deal with him at St. Agnes, he is the Co-op member most likely to turn — and he knows the Bell's route card by heart.

rewards.money: About $2,600 in cash on the escorts and in the Dutch Hollow camp office, which is now worth nothing at all. The Co-op Market chalkboard reads CASH NOT ACCEPTED. Children at Prairie Hill are folding twenties into paper boats.

Prairie Hill trade: Supplies (+20 to +30 person-days), 2 laying hens, Coffee (1 pound)
Dutch Hollow pantry: canned goods (25 person-days)
Sullivan quarry shack: Co-op handheld radio, 12-gauge shells (14), .308 rounds (20)
The Bell (if captured): the truck, the siren, the generator, Diesel (30 gallons)
Wade Pruitt's kit: AR-15, 5.56mm rounds (60), Glock 9mm, 9mm rounds (30), plate carrier
Escort pickups: 2 Ford F-250s, Gasoline (30 gallons total), 12-gauge shells (18), 9mm rounds (40), .308 rounds (12), Co-op radio
The green ledger, if taken: the Co-op's own record of every holdout, every assessment, and every 'Rung'
rewards.story: Prairie Hill stands, and owes the party everything. The Co-op has lost its driver, maybe its Bell, maybe its pen, and knows exactly who to blame. The party knows what Colleen Marsh is, and has some combination of proof (the ledger), a weapon (the Bell) and a witness (Wade, Caleb, Travis). Ammunition is less desperate for the first time since Day 1, thanks to the reloading supplies. And somewhere north, upriver, there is a lot more coming.

twists: Dutch Hollow was not bad luck. The Co-op rang it: the Bell led three hundred dead from the quarry pen to a camp that refused its assessment, and cut the gate chain first.
Wade Pruitt, the friendliest man the party has met since Day 1, drives the Bell. He believes he is saving more people than he kills, and by Colleen's arithmetic, he is.

Nadine Coyle signed a request for Co-op protection on Day 4, during a frightening night, without asking the bishop. Colleen holds it as Prairie Hill's consent to the assessment. Nadine has told no one.

Most of the Co-op's eleven hundred members do not know what the Bell is for. They think the siren truck is for 'clearing roads'. The green ledger is the only written proof otherwise — and Colleen keeps it on her desk because she is not ashamed of it.

Walt Hennessey's farm is on Old Mill Road, a quarter mile off County Road K between Sullivan Ridge and Prairie Hill. The Bell's route passes it. If the party sets up their ambush at the Lindell farm or scouts the road, they hear something chained in Walt's barn — his wife Ellen, who died of a stroke on Day 1 and rose. (See his NPC file.) Let Walt be there when they find her.
If Shay Pruitt is with the party, Wade is her brother, and she has been passing him small, harmless news about the party since ob-scenario-002 so that he would leave them alone. (See her NPC file.)
dmTips: Run Colleen Marsh as reasonable, competent and right about the numbers. The horror is not that she is wrong about the arithmetic. It is what she does about it.
Use the Market to showcase the Scarcity and Barter rule: the chalkboard is the rule. Let the players haggle in rounds of ammunition.
Do not let the party start a war inside the Co-op perimeter in Act 2. Tell them plainly that thirty guards and a sniper on a 140-foot tower is not a fight, it is an ending.

The Bell is a set-piece built for clever play: the cab switch (one action), the bridge planks (an hour's work), the sealed pen (a truck and a Piloting check), Wade's surrender (a person he trusts). Reward every one of those over shooting.
Be honest about scale. Six Hordes walking behind a siren is not a fight a level-4 party can win, and the GM should describe it so they know that before they try.
When the Bell goes silent, the dead drift toward the next-loudest thing. Use that: it is how the party's own gunfire becomes the threat.

Wade Pruitt alive is worth more to the campaign than Wade dead. If the players capture him, play him as a man who believes he is decent, frightened of Colleen and of himself. If they kill him, remember he rises.
Track Prairie Hill as a holdout with a headcount. If the party saves it, it becomes their ally in ob-scenario-004: food, horses, a place to evacuate to.
The level 4 to 5 jump happens here. Award XP at the end of each act, not only at the end.
